thread.title: US STOCKS-Tech keeps Nasdaq, S&P under pressure; industrials lift Dow Reuters

author: Reuters
title: US STOCKS-Tech keeps Nasdaq, S&P under pressure; industrials lift Dow Reuters
text:
© Reuters. US STOCKS-Tech keeps Nasdaq, S&P under pressure; industrials lift Dow * Allergan (NYSE: AGN ) drops as 2019 forecast misses estimates
* Harley-Davidson tumbles on 4th-qtr profit miss
* 3M (NYSE: MMM ), defense companies lead industrial stocks higher
* Apple inches higher ahead of earnings
* Dow up 0.28 pct, S&P off 0.14 pct, Nasdaq down 0.69 pct
(Updates to early afternoon)
By Sruthi Shankar
Jan 29 (Reuters) - The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq came under pressure from weakness in technology stocks ahead of Apple's results on Tuesday, while a rebound in industrial stocks lifted the Dow.
U.S. stocks tumbled on Monday as profit alerts from Caterpillar Inc (NYSE: CAT ) CAT.N and Nvidia Corp NVDA.O raised fears that a slowdown in China and tariffs could take a bigger hit on profits.
Industrial stocks .SPLRCI , which took a beating after Caterpillar's warning on Monday, rose 1.1 percent, helped by upbeat reports for 3M Co MMM.N and defense companies.
Technology stocks .SPLRCT fell 0.8 percent, weighed down by chipmakers and Microsoft Corp MSFT.O .
Apple Inc AAPL.O , set to report after market close on Tuesday, was trading flat. The iPhone maker earlier this month took the rare step of cutting its quarterly sales forecast, blaming slowing sales in China, whose economy has been dragged down by a tit-for-tat tariff war with the United States.
"There's a cautious approach today," said Paul Brigandi, Managing Director and Head of Trading at Direxion. "No one wants to place any large bets ahead of big events like the jobs report, the Fed meeting, the U.S.-China tariff negotiations along with it being the biggest week for earnings,"
As Washington and Beijing officials prepare for a high-level trade meeting this week, the Justice Department leveled charges against China's telecom giant Huawei HWT.UL , potentially casting a cloud on the talks. Federal Reserve begins its two-day monetary policy meeting on Tuesday. After raising rates gradually last year, the central bank is taking a wait-and-see approach to further tightening in the face of an overseas slowdown and market volatility. 1:08 p.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was up 69.17 points, or 0.28 percent, at 24,597.39, the S&P 500 .SPX was down 3.65 points, or 0.14 percent, at 2,640.20 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was down 48.96 points, or 0.69 percent, at 7,036.72.
Amazon.com Inc AMZN.O , Facebook Inc FB.O and Microsoft, all scheduled to report later this week, fell more than 2 percent.
Four of the 11 major S&P sectors were lower. The S&P communication services index .SPLRCL fell 0.88 percent, dragged down by wireless carrier Verizon Communications Inc (NYSE: VZ ) VZ.N , which dipped 2.5 percent after missing quarterly revenue estimates. contractors L3 Technologies Inc LLL.N rose 7 percent and Harris Corp (NYSE: HRS ) HRS.N climbed 7.4 percent after topping quarterly earnings estimates.
3M rose 1.8 percent after fourth-quarter results topped estimates, but the Post-It notes maker trimmed 2019 earnings outlook, saying that a slowdown at its Chinese business was hurting revenue. Inc HOG.N dropped 7.7 percent after the motorcycle maker reported a lower-than-expected quarterly profit, hit by declining sales in the United States. Plc AGN.N fell 7.5 percent after the Botox maker forecast 2019 revenue below expectations. issues outnumbered decliners for a 1.47-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. Declining issues outnumbered advancers for a 1.16-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P index recorded 10 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq recorded 23 new highs and 21 new lows.
